name: Question 15
problem:
The total number of people $V(t)$ who have visited a certain shopping center after $t$ hours is given by the function

$$
V(t)=1\,000+100{\int }_{0}^{t}(2x-6)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time (in hours) since the shopping center opened its doors to the public.

At what time is the number of people visiting the shopping center at a minimum, and how many people are in the shopping center at that time?
worked_solution:
To find when the number of people is at minimum, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1\,000+100{\int }_{0}^{t}(2x-6)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1\,000)+100\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({\int }_{0}^{t}(2x-6)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =100\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(2x-6)\,\text{d}x \\  & =100(2t-6)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=0$:

$$
100(2t-6)=0\,⟹\,t=3
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=3.$ To find out how many people are in the shopping center when $t=3,$ we figure out $V(3)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}V(3) & =1\,000+100{\int }_{0}^{3}(2x-6)\,\text{d}x \\  & =1\,000+100{[{x}^{2}-6x]|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =1\,000+100[({3}^{2}-6(3))-(0)] \\  & =1\,000-900 \\  & =100\end{aligned}
$$

Since $100<1\,000$, we conclude that the minimum number of people is $100$, and this will happen after $3$ hours.

html:
Question 15
?

The total number of people V(t) who have visited a certain shopping center after t hours is given by the function

V(t)=1000+100∫0t(2x−6)dx,

where t>0 is the time (in hours) since the shopping center opened its doors to the public.

At what time is the number of people visiting the shopping center at a minimum, and how many people are in the shopping center at that time?

a
The minimum is 500 people after 1 hour
b
The minimum is 150 people after 5 hours
c
The minimum is 100 people after 3 hours
d
The minimum is 200 people after 2 hours
e
The minimum is 200 people after 4 hours
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find when the number of people is at minimum, we need to solve dVdt=0. First, we differentiate:

dVdt=ddt(1000+100∫0t(2x−6)dx)=ddt(1000)+100ddt(∫0t(2x−6)dx)=100ddt∫0t(2x−6)dx=100(2t−6)

Now, we solve dVdt=0:

100(2t−6)=0⟹t=3

So there are two candidates for global extrema, t=0 and t=3. To find out how many people are in the shopping center when t=3, we figure out V(3):

V(3)=1000+100∫03(2x−6)dx=1000+100[x2−6x]|03=1000+100[(32−6(3))−(0)]=1000−900=100

Since 100<1000, we conclude that the minimum number of people is 100, and this will happen after 3 hours.
